speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: I see you're experiencing sudden vertigo; to better understand your condition, can you tell me if you have any hearing loss, tinnitus, or a sensation of fullness in your ears on the affected side?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Given the brief duration (3 minutes) and absence of auditory symptoms like hearing loss or tinnitus, BPPV is the most likely cause. Would you like me to perform the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm this?
